# System Reference

> How systems actually work — seen, not read. Visual, interactive references for architects, developers and testers: APIs, databases, identity, cloud, networking and more — explained with diagrams you can click, drag and study.

System Reference explains how systems actually work with visual, interactive reference guides. Each guide includes a detailed written breakdown plus mermaid and interactive flow diagrams. Browse by role (developer, backend, frontend, tester, enterprise architect, solution architect, data architect, security architect, network engineer, endpoint device engineer, cloud engineer, DevOps engineer) or by topic.

## Guide index

- [API request lifecycle](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/api-request-lifecycle): Follow one HTTP request as it crosses the gateway, application, cache, and database — and trace how the response finds its way back. (developer, backend, tester · #api #architecture #performance)
- [AsyncAPI](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/asyncapi): The OpenAPI equivalent for event-driven architectures: define message payloads, channels, protocols, and bindings so producers and consumers stay in sync — with code generation, documentation, and governance built in. (developer, backend, enterprise-architect, solution-architect, data-architect · #api #architecture #messaging #event-driven)
- [Blockchain Fundamentals](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/blockchain-fundamentals): Distributed ledgers, cryptographic hashes, consensus mechanisms, and immutability — the primitives that let mutually distrusting nodes share state without a central authority. (developer, solution-architect, security-architect, cloud-engineer, enterprise-architect · #blockchain #decentralization #distributed-systems #cryptography #ledger #immutability)
- [Card networks at scale](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/card-networks-at-scale): How Visa and Mastercard process tens of thousands of transactions per second: the switch, ISO 8583, authorization latency budgets, clearing and settlement at volume. (solution-architect, enterprise-architect, backend, data-architect, tester · #payments #cards #architecture #scalability #finance)
- [Core banking systems](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/core-banking-systems): The account-and-ledger backbone of a bank: who owns what money, how a transaction moves it, double-entry posting, and the difference between real-time and overnight processing. (solution-architect, data-architect, enterprise-architect, backend, tester · #banking #ledgers #finance #transaction-processing #architecture)
- [Database indexing](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/database-indexing): How a B-tree index turns a table scan into a happy few millisecond lookups — and when an index hurts instead of helps. (developer, backend, tester · #database #performance)
- [Decentralized Identity and Verifiable Credentials](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/decentralized-identity-and-verifiable-credentials): Self-sovereign identity: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), verifiable credentials, and the issuer-holder-verifier triangle replacing centralized account databases. (security-architect, solution-architect, developer, enterprise-architect, tester · #identity #decentralization #verifiable-credentials #ssi #cryptography #blockchain)
- [E-commerce platform architecture](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/ecommerce-platform-architecture): Storefront to store room: catalog, cart, checkout, payments, order management, fulfillment, and the returns loop — and where the money lands in the ERP. (solution-architect, developer, frontend, backend, tester, data-architect · #ecommerce #retail #payments #integration #web #workflow)
- [FedRAMP and NIST Risk Management Framework](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/fedramp-nist-rmf): How government systems get authority to operate: the NIST RMF lifecycle, SP 800-53 control families and impact levels, FedRAMP for cloud services, and the ATO decision. (security-architect, enterprise-architect, solution-architect · #compliance #security #federal #governance #cloud)
- [Government identity: PIV/CAC and NIST 800-63](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/government-identity-piv-ficam): Federal identity done right: PIV and CAC cards, FICAM architecture, NIST 800-63 identity assurance levels (IAL/AAL), and how agencies, contractors, and citizens get verified once and federate everywhere. (security-architect, solution-architect, enterprise-architect · #identity #federal #security #zero-trust #compliance)
- [Grants management life-cycle](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/grants-management-life-cycle): The full life of an award: opportunity announcement, application, merit review, award, performance reporting, drawdown, and closeout — with the compliance obligations unique to federal and state funding. (enterprise-architect, solution-architect, data-architect, tester · #grants #federal #governance #compliance #workflow #funding)
- [Kubernetes and container orchestration](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/kubernetes-and-container-orchestration): The control plane and data plane of running containers at scale: pods, deployments, services, scheduling and self-healing, networking, storage, and when Kubernetes is the right (and wrong) answer. (cloud-engineer, devops-engineer, developer, backend, solution-architect · #kubernetes #containers #orchestration #devops #cloud #platform)
- [LLM RAG pipeline](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/llm-rag-pipeline): Retrieval-augmented generation: embedding, vector search, and how a prompt gets grounded in your own data instead of the model’s memory. (developer, backend, tester · #ai #database #api #architecture)
- [Mainframe computing](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/mainframe-computing): The mainframe that still runs the world's money: z/OS architecture, batch versus online CICS, COBOL, JCL, and the strangler strategy for modernizing without switching it off. (solution-architect, enterprise-architect, backend, data-architect, devops-engineer · #mainframe #legacy #zos #modernization #architecture)
- [Payments, clearing, and settlement](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/payments-clearing-and-settlement): The rails that move money between banks: payment schemes, clearing house mechanics, netting, settlement risk, and ISO 20022 messages. (solution-architect, enterprise-architect, backend, tester · #banking #payments #settlement #iso20022 #finance)
- [Quantum computing fundamentals](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/quantum-computing-fundamentals): Qubits, superposition, entanglement, gates, and error correction — what quantum computers actually compute, where they beat classical hardware, and what the architecture looks like today. (solution-architect, enterprise-architect, developer, security-architect · #quantum #computing #cryptography #architecture #emerging)
- [SASE and SSE](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/sase): Secure Access Service Edge: SD-WAN plus cloud-native security (SWG, CASB, ZTNA, FWaaS) delivered as a global cloud service from nearby Points of Presence. (security-architect, network-engineer, cloud-engineer, enterprise-architect · #security #network #cloud #identity #zero-trust)
- [Smart Contracts and Decentralized Apps](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/smart-contracts-and-decentralized-apps): Smart contracts, wallets, tokens, and dApp frontends — how programmable logic and self-custody put application state on an open, incentive-aligned blockchain. (developer, frontend, backend, tester, solution-architect, security-architect · #web3 #smart-contracts #tokens #wallets #decentralization #blockchain)
- [The OWASP Top 10](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/owasp-top-10): The ten riskiest web-application security weaknesses, the attacks that trigger them, and the fixes that stop them before a pentest finds them. (developer, backend, tester, security-architect · #security #api #architecture #planning)
- [Threat modeling with STRIDE](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/threat-modeling-stride): A repeatable way to find design flaws before they become exploits — diagram your system, enumerate threats with STRIDE, then rank and mitigate. (security-architect, solution-architect, tester · #security #architecture #planning)
- [TOGAF and the ADM](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/togaf-framework): The Architecture Development Method: a repeatable 8-phase cycle for moving from architecture vision to implemented, governed change. (enterprise-architect, solution-architect · #architecture #enterprise-architecture #planning)
- [Zero Trust architecture](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/zero-trust-architecture): Never trust, always verify — identity-aware, micro-segmented networks that assume breach instead of defending a perimeter. (security-architect, enterprise-architect, solution-architect · #security #architecture #enterprise-architecture #zero-trust)
- [Android in the enterprise](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/android-in-the-enterprise): EMM and work profiles: separating personal from corporate on BYOD, fully managed COPE devices, and provisioning via QR/NFC. (endpoint-device-engineer, security-architect, developer · #endpoint #security #mobile)
- [API gateway caching](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/api-gateway-caching): Cache-control headers, stale-while-revalidate, and cache keys — use the interactive diagram to poke at where a response can be served from. (developer, backend, frontend, tester · #api #performance #architecture)
- [Authentication vs authorization](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/authentication-vs-authorization): The two questions every request must answer — who are you, and what are you allowed to do — and why conflating them is a classic breach. (developer, backend, tester, security-architect · #security #api #architecture)
- [AWS core services](https://lvdatri1.github.io/architect-reference-site/systems/aws-core-services): VPC, EC2, Lambda, S3, RDS, IAM — the map of core AWS services and how a web app fits inside them. (cloud-engineer, backend, solution-architect · #cloud #aws #architecture)
